summary: Don village's own monsoon waterfall. A 1–2 km walk to a pool-bottomed drop, with changing rooms at the base and a genuinely rough approach road.
description:
The plateau village of Don keeps a waterfall in its back pocket: a monsoon cascade a short trek from the village, dropping into a natural pool that draws weekend bathers from across the district. The walk in runs one to two kilometres, easy-to-moderate, and the base has grown a small welcome, changing rooms, washrooms, tea and snack sellers, which makes it one of the more visitor-ready of Dang's remote falls.

The catch is the approach: the road toward the falls is regularly described as bad and unsuited to low cars, and it compounds the already-steep final climb to Don village itself. Come in a high-clearance vehicle or accept a longer walk. Weekends in August get properly busy with local crowds; weekdays return the falls to the herders.

It completes the Don day perfectly, meadows and ridgelines up top, the pool below, and pairs with Birsa waterfall on the drive back toward Ahwa.
highlights: Natural pool at the base, the district's favourite monsoon dip
1–2 km easy-to-moderate walk from Don village
Changing rooms and tea stalls at the base

modes.road: Via the Don village road from Ahwa; the waterfall stretch is rough and not friendly to low cars
modes.rail: No practical railhead; Waghai/Bilimora serve the district

access.last_mile: 1–2 km walk from the parking/base area; easy to moderate
access.road_condition: Steep, narrow and broken in stretches, high clearance helps

timings.note: Managed informally in season; daylight only

visit.notes: August weekends run crowded with local visitors; weekdays are quiet.

seasonality.notes: A monsoon waterfall in practice. Flow thins fast from November.

experience.photography_notes: The pool bowl shoots best late morning when light clears the rim; keep gear dry-bagged in spray.

amenities.food: Tea and snack sellers at the base in season; meals at Don village or Ahwa
amenities.guides: Village youths point the way for a small tip

warnings: Enter the pool only in gentle flow and never alone, depth and currents change with every rain
The approach road is genuinely bad; avoid after-dark driving
Rocks around the pool are slick, grip footwear, not slippers

tips: Do the plateau at dawn, the waterfall before noon, and Birsa on the drive back
Carry a change of clothes: the changing rooms assume you'll need them
Weekdays beat August Sundays by a wide margin

faqs.q: Can you swim at Don waterfall?
faqs.a: Locals do, in the calmer pool edges and in moderate flow. Treat it with monsoon respect: currents strengthen after rain, and there is no lifeguard, never swim alone or in spate.

nearby.note: Same plateau, fold both into the Don day
On the Ahwa side, natural pairing
